title: FBI co-Deputy Director Andrew Bailey steps down after one year on the job
summary: FBI co-Deputy Director Andrew Bailey, who joined the FBI in the newly created position in September 2025 to work alongside then-Deputy Director Dan Bongino, is stepping down, two people familiar with the matter told NBC News.
story: WASHINGTON — Another top FBI official is leaving the bureau after just a year on the job.

Andrew Bailey, who joined the FBI in the newly created position of “co-deputy director” in September 2025 to work alongside then-Deputy Director Dan Bongino, is stepping aside, two people familiar with the matter told NBC News. Bailey confirmed his move later Monday morning on social media.

An internal FBI email said Bailey was leaving for family reasons, the two people familiar with the matter said. Bailey had been the attorney general of Missouri before resigning his position to join the FBI last year. He had worked under FBI Director Kash Patel.
The FBI referred a request for comment to a post Bailey made on social media, stating that he wanted to thank President Donald Trump, Attorney General Todd Blanche and Patel for the opportunity.

“Under President Trump’s leadership, we have delivered historic results in our mission to Make America Safe Again. With great pride in what we have accomplished, I am announcing that I am stepping down to return to my family in Missouri,” Bailey wrote. “I am confident Director Patel will continue to reform the FBI, combat violent crime, defend the homeland, ensure strong organizational accountability, and restore public trust in this institution of excellence.”

Bongino, a conservative podcaster and former Secret Service member, subsequently left his job to return to podcasting after just under a year at the FBI. The nontraditional co-deputy structure, set up when Bongino was in the position, remained in place. Bongino was then replaced by Chris Raia, whose background as a career FBI special agent was more in line with the tradition of having the critical No. 2 position filled by someone with extensive knowledge of the bureau.
MS NOW first reported Bailey’s planned departure.

Patel, who is suing The Atlantic for $250 million over an article about his leadership at the bureau, has recently gotten into heated exchanges with Democratic members of Congress over his leadership at the FBI.

title: Right-wing conservatives push to shut down the last active Jan. 6 prosecution
summary: They say Brian Cole Jr. was framed. The Justice Department is pressing forward with the case.
story: WASHINGTON — There’s just one active federal prosecution still tied to the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol, the case of the man accused of planting two pipe bombs near the Republican National Committee and the Democratic National Committee. And some of MAGA’s most fervent supporters want to shut it down.

Some conservative figures accuse the Trump administration of framing Brian Cole Jr., who was arrested almost five years after the unexploded devices were placed. Cole, as NBC News first reported, told the FBI that he believed the 2020 election had been stolen after false accusations fueled by President Donald Trump and his supporters.

Cole has pleaded not guilty, and a trial is set for February. The FBI said he confessed after his arrest, but his legal team has noted that he was diagnosed with autism and is expected to seek to have the confession tossed based on his disability or argue he was coerced.

The prosecution has opened a rift between the Trump administration and some prominent right-wing conservatives who are seeking to undermine the case by spreading discredited theories about who was to blame. They contend the bombs were placed by “deep state” actors to distract from the police response and make Jan. 6 seem more violent.
Right-wing activists have appeared in court to support Cole, and former Jan. 6 defendants are backing him online.

Trump pardoned Jan. 6 defendants as one of his first acts in office, and as a result, the Justice Department shut down ongoing investigations into the rioters who beat and bloodied law enforcement and caused an estimated $2.7 billion in costs.

Legally, federal prosecutors pushed forward with the pipe bomb case because the devices were placed the night before the attack and therefore the crime wasn’t covered under Trump’s mass Jan. 6 pardon. The devices were viable but didn’t explode, law enforcement said.

Culturally, it’s been a right-wing talking point for years. In a 2024 podcast, Dan Bongino said he had “zero doubt” the bombs were an inside job. When Bongino became the FBI’s deputy director, he pushed the stalled investigation forward. During the announcement of Cole’s arrest, then-Attorney General Pam Bondi credited him with helping crack the case.

Bongino, who left the bureau in January, has not directly addressed how — or whether — his opinions on the “inside job” theory have changed. After the December arrest, he told Fox News commentator Sean Hannity in an interview: “I was paid in the past, Sean, for my opinions, that’s clear, and one day I will be back in that space — but that’s not what I’m paid for now.”

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., publicly posted a photo of officials — including Bondi, U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro, FBI Director Kash Patel and Bongino — at the news conference announcing Cole’s arrest and said they were “complicit” in a conspiracy.

“The evidence is mounting,” Massie said on social media. “All of the people who took credit at the podium upon the arrest of Brian Cole Jr. are complicit, either through negligence or malfeasance. Mr. Cole is not the J5/J6 pipe bomber, and the identity of the actual perpetrator is being obscured. Bookmark it.”

title: White House releases new taxpayer-funded ad describing ‘final battle’
summary: The ad is nearly identical to one Trump’s presidential campaign released in 2024.
story: The Trump administration put out a new ad this weekend as part of its “PSA” campaign, this time showing President Donald Trump walking down a hallway as he asks people to join him in his fight to “expel the warmongers from our government.”
The ad — which at the end says it was “Paid for by the U.S. government” — is nearly identical to an ad put out by Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign.

Trump posted that ad to Truth Social in January 2024. The repurposed ad now includes “Paid for by the U.S. government.” But it excludes the last few seconds of the 2024 ad, which ends with text reading “Join President Trump’s fight to save America” and his 2024 campaign logo.

The ad signals an expansion of the White House’s controversial use of government funds to air pieces that resemble campaign advertisements. Last week, the White House ran a television ad in which Trump described how he wanted to “defeat communism,” set to the song “Love Me” by JMSN. The White House has called the ads “public service announcements.”

In the latest ad, dramatic black-and-white video shows President Trump walking down a hallway with audio of him saying it is the “final battle” and vowing to “demolish the deep state” and “throw off the sick political class that hates our country.”
“We will rout the fake news media, and we will liberate America from these villains once and for all,” it concludes.

Federal law requires political advertisers to submit certain public disclosures and generally bans using public funds for political advertising. Since the administration maintains the ads are public service announcements, it’s not clear whether those disclosures are available. The White House has not released a specific source of government funding used to air the ads.

AdImpact, a political ad tracking firm, has estimated that the administration has spent more than $1.7 million to run these ads, which have been running heavily in recent days during prominent television programming like football games, Sunday morning news shows, and prime time broadcast shows. That said, AdImpact doesn’t have full visibility into airings on every cable channel in every market in the country, hampering that estimate.
The White House defended the ad Sunday, pointing NBC News to a statement it had offered last week when it commented on the other ads released by the administration.

“These public service announcements are about reminding Americans to love their country and understand what makes it worth defending, at home, at our borders, and abroad. The ad is educational and unapologetically patriotic. We should be proud of our country,” a White House spokesperson said.
Another White House official pushed back on the line of questioning: “The PSAs are clearly not political. The president is not on the ballot, and the ads don’t have a call to action.”
The White House did not specifically respond to NBC News’ question about the ad’s being nearly identical to the 2024 Trump campaign ad.

A White House spokesperson also pointed to past examples of ads released by former administrations, including an ad by George W. Bush’s Department of Health and Human Services, a social media campaign by Barack Obama’s Environmental Protection Agency in 2014 and 2015 and an effort by Joe Biden’s administration encouraging Covid-19 vaccination.

The nonpartisan Government Accountability Office dinged the Bush and Obama ad campaigns — Bush’s for not properly disclosing the government was the source and Obama’s for violating “publicity or propaganda and anti-lobbying provisions.”

White House communications director Steven Cheung defended the recent pro-Trump ads Sunday on social media, writing, “Don’t let the Fake News get away with their lies about our epic Public Service Announcements that have been running on tv.”
CNN and The New York Times were first to report about the ad’s being almost identical to Trump’s 2024 campaign ad.
Spending taxpayer dollars on the ads has raised legal and ethical concerns and condemnation from both parties.

“This is the sort of government propaganda one might expect in North Korea, not the United States of America, and it is an egregious and utterly illegal misuse of Americans’ hard-earned tax dollars,” congressional Democratic appropriators wrote in a letter Friday addressed to White House chief of staff Susie Wiles.
The letter was signed by Sen. Patty Murray, D-Wash.; Sen. Jack Reed, D-R.I.; Rep. Rosa De Lauro, D-Conn.; and Rep. Steny Hoyer, D-Md.
Sen. John Kennedy, R-La., said Sunday in an interview with CBS that public officials should not “spend public money on private ads for themselves.”

title: The dozen games that turned Week 3 into one of the wildest in NFL history
summary: Two seconds remained in regulation in Denver.
story: Two seconds remained in regulation in Denver. One final play to decide the game.
Could one of the wildest Sundays in NFL history have ended any other way?

When Denver safety Talanoa Hufanga intercepted Los Angeles Rams quarterback Matthew Stafford in the end zone as time expired to seal a 30-26 comeback win on “Sunday Night Football,” it also capped a day that will be remembered for producing one thriller after another.

Call it the Sunday of slim margins. Of the day’s 14-game slate in Week 3, 12 finished as one-score games, the most on any Sunday in NFL history. Thirteen games were within 8 points during the fourth quarter. Six teams won after go-ahead scores within the final three minutes.
“It’s tough,” Rams coach Sean McVay said. “But this is sports.”

After watching two weeks of offensive struggles under Denver’s new play caller, Broncos fans booed their team as they ran off the field after trailing the Rams, 16-0, at halftime. Then Denver scored 16 unanswered points, setting up a fourth quarter where the teams traded momentum swings. Hufanga intercepted Stafford and ran it back for a touchdown to lead, 23-19. When a Broncos defensive back fell down on the next possession, Stafford found an open receiver for an easy, go-ahead touchdown to lead, 26-23. Denver came back and moved the ball down the field after a succession of penalties, eventually taking a 30-26 lead and leaving the preseason Super Bowl favorite Rams only 47 seconds with which to try their own rally.
It fell short by only a few yards, with no time left to spare — and it might not have even been Sunday’s wildest finish.

In Rio de Janeiro, Baltimore got the ball back with seven seconds to play in regulation after Dallas had tied the score. Somehow, that was enough time for the Ravens to launch perhaps the latest comeback drive ever — at least since one database began tracking such figures — ending in Baltimore’s walk-off field goal from 56 yards. It was the first game since the 1970 merger to feature two teams that each made a field goal in the final 10 seconds.
Improbable? It wasn’t the only game that fit the description.

Previously winless, Washington couldn’t run the ball or convert third downs against Seattle yet knocked off the defending Super Bowl champion anyway, behind backup quarterback Marcus Mariota’s three touchdowns and three Seahawks turnovers. It ended the Seahawks’ 12-game winning streak and temporarily halted their historic run as the NFL’s best road team.

In New Orleans, the Las Vegas Raiders improved to 3-0 after a 35-27 victory that saw the franchise match last season’s entire win total. They are now only the seventh team since the 1970 merger to open 3-0 after finishing the previous season with the league’s worst record, according to NBC Sports research.

The Raiders pulled it off after trailing by 11 points in the second half. A controversial fumble call on Saints quarterback Tyler Shough helped the Raiders set up their go-ahead touchdown, but it was just one of four consecutive Saints turnovers forced by the Raiders in the second half.
“In those big moments, there’s no panic,” Raiders defensive end Maxx Crosby said. “We went down 11 and got together on the sideline and talked about not panicking.”

Neither did the Bills (3-0). Like Baltimore and Las Vegas, Buffalo overcame a deficit of at least 10 points, eventually beating the Los Angeles Chargers, 24-16. It was the first time since 1997 that the Bills won a game despite committing at least five turnovers. Bills quarterback Josh Allen hadn’t committed a single turnover through two weeks, only to be intercepted twice and lose a fumble against Los Angeles (0-3).

If Allen’s poor play was unexpected considering how good he had looked in MVP-level performances to begin the season, then what happened in Cleveland was the opposite. After ranking among the least efficient quarterbacks in the league for much of his tenure in Cleveland, Deshaun Watson has suddenly looked competent — and the Browns are now 2-1, after a 21-18 win. Watson threw two touchdowns, including a go-ahead score with 1:48 left in the fourth quarter. An interception of Carolina’s Bryce Young with seconds remaining clinched Watson’s 10th fourth-quarter comeback.

Indianapolis (1-2) earned its first win since last November after Spencer Shrader kicked a 43-yard field goal with 16 seconds left for a 19-17 victory that dumps Houston, a preseason Super Bowl candidate, to 0-3. The Texans made the playoffs last year after starting 0-3, too, becoming only the seventh team in NFL history to do so. Another hard road to the playoffs awaits.

In whipping rain and wind in New Jersey, the New York Giants held on for a 12-7 win in their first game since quarterback Jaxson Dart suffered a season-ending knee injury. Sack artist Brian Burns injured his knee in the fourth quarter, and with 24 seconds left in regulation, Tennessee moved within 7 yards of a go-ahead touchdown. Instead, the Giants (2-1) survived after Jevon Holland intercepted Titans quarterback Cam Ward.

In Tampa Bay, the Buccaneers played in their franchise-record ninth consecutive one-score game, but Minnesota (3-0) held on, 23-16, after batting down a desperate Hail Mary heave as time expired. For Tampa, what was even more dispiriting than falling to 0-3 was that quarterback Baker Mayfield left with a dislocated thumb that puts his active league-high streak of 54 consecutive starts in jeopardy.

When Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow fumbled late in the fourth quarter, Pittsburgh exhaled with a 30-27 win over a division rival. It also breathed a sigh of relief for a different reason. Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, the NFL’s oldest active player, was showing his age. He entered Sunday having gone seven consecutive starts without throwing multiple touchdown passes. He responded with touchdown passes to three different receivers and led Pittsburgh (2-1) on a game-winning drive that ended with a 33-yard field goal with 2:15 remaining. Burrow’s fumble occurred just before the Bengals (2-1) could reach field-goal range of their own.

With one game remaining in Week 3, six teams remain undefeated after San Francisco edged out a 36-30 win over Arizona. Can the 49ers keep it up, though? A franchise known for suffering a rash of injuries got more bad news Sunday when receiver Mike Evans (ribs) and left tackle Trent Williams (stinger) left the game.

That left the Broncos and Rams to play a vital primetime game — the two Super Bowl contenders each hoping to avoid a second loss within their first three weeks. A pair of controversial defensive pass interference penalties on Denver’s go-ahead drive in the final minute rankled the Rams after the game, but comebacks have become something of a Broncos specialty.

Last season, the Broncos’ 12 comeback wins set an NFL record. Last week, Denver overcame a 10-point deficit to beat Jacksonville. Sunday’s latest rally was the 50th fourth-quarter comeback of coach Sean Payton’s career to move past Mike Tomlin for fourth-most in NFL history. It relied on the 20th touchdown of quarterback Bo Nix’s career when trailing by one score — the most in the league since 2025, when Nix entered the NFL — and resulted in Nix’s seventh career fourth-quarter comeback.
“Just a couple plays short that we left out there,” Rams receiver Konata Mumpfield said.
On a day of wild finishes and tight margins, it was a sentiment shared across the league.

title: How an American teacher’s $5,000 donation helped turn a Chinese desert into a lush forest
summary: Ronald Sakolsky couldn’t believe his eyes when he visited China’s Mu Us Desert for the first time in 26 years. “Seeing it with my own eyes, that was the biggest surprise,” he said.
story: HONG KONG — Ronald Sakolsky never thought his money would go this far.

What was once a vast, dry desert in northern China has transformed into a lush, green forest of 50,000 full-grown trees, thanks in part to a $5,000 donation he made more than a quarter-century ago to a local farmer and “sand-control worker” named Yin Yuzhen.
Sakolsky, 69, a retired teacher from Pennsylvania, was amazed to see the transformation in China’s Inner Mongolia region last month when he visited for the first time in 26 years.
“Seeing it with my own eyes, that was the biggest surprise,” he told Chinese state media. “I saw pictures, I was told all about it, but until you see it is when you realize that it’s real.”

Sakolsky and Yin’s reunion last month has been held up by Chinese authorities as an example of how China and the United States, the world’s two biggest greenhouse gas emitters, can work together on global issues such as climate change.

Chinese leader Xi Jinping, in Washington this week for a summit with President Donald Trump, mentioned Sakolsky’s story in his toast at a state dinner on Thursday, saying it “touches the hearts of many Chinese people and stands as a shining example of the friendly exchanges between our two peoples.”

Sakolsky was teaching English on exchange in China’s central Henan province in 1999 when he saw a TV news report about Yin. More than a decade earlier, the newly married Yin had started planting trees as a way to feel less isolated in her new home in the Mu Us Desert, also known as the Maowusu Desert (“bad water” in Mongolian).

Moved by her story, Sakolsky raised $5,000, which was many times Yin’s annual income, so she could plant even more. They met in person in 2000, when Yin promised Sakolsky that she and her family would take good care of the saplings.

title: Europe frets as the Kremlin pushes the limits of its hybrid warfare
summary: The Kremlin is testing Europe‘s limits.
story: The Kremlin is testing Europe‘s limits.
After months of covert attacks and sabotage across the continent, leaders are warning that Moscow may be about to grow bolder as it seeks to sow chaos and intimidate allies of Ukraine.

Russian President Vladimir Putin could try to test NATO’s resolve to defend members on its eastern flank or respond to attacks that fall short of all-out war, these officials say, at a time when the U.S. is distracted by other conflicts and weighing reducing its military presence in Europe.

An assessment by the Danish Defence Intelligence Service released Thursday warned that in the coming months Moscow will further intensify its campaign of so-called hybrid warfare, “with greater consequences for the targeted countries than in the past.” It also assessed “a low but growing risk that Russia will launch a limited military attack against one or several NATO countries bordering Russia.”
While Moscow has for years embraced tactics that straddle the threshold of war, a string of increasingly brazen incidents in recent months has alarmed U.S. allies.
‘A bit freaked out’

A key moment was the discovery of a Russian drone carrying explosives at an airport in eastern Germany near a Ukrainian aircraft last month. Berlin formally blamed Russia for what it said was a thwarted attack and imposed a diplomatic freeze, though Moscow denied involvement.

That incident appears to have changed the mindset about Russia’s growing threat in Europe, said Ed Arnold, a senior associate fellow in international security at the Royal United Services Institute, a London-based think tank. “It just showed that Putin’s risk calculations are getting more liberal,” Arnold said. “Everyone just got a bit freaked out by that, quite frankly.”
It was followed by the unexpected visit of CIA Director John Ratcliffe to Moscow, during which NATO was discussed.

Incidents have continued to pile up — at defense facilities in Estonia, rail networks in Poland and the power grid in Germany. Many have passed without clear attribution, only intensifying speculation.
All this against the backdrop of near-daily drone incursions into European airspace, fueling anxiety in eastern border towns.

title: Stocks fall, oil rises and bond yields surge as geopolitics keeps markets on edge
summary: Stocks fell on Monday alongside jumps in both bond yields and the price of oil as geopolitical upheaval remained front and center for traders.
story: Stocks fell on Monday alongside jumps in both bond yields and the price of oil as geopolitical upheaval remained front and center for traders.
The S&P 500 fell 0.5% and the Nasdaq Composite dropped 0.6% as oil prices staged a 3% rally, pushing Brent crude oil to nearly $108 per barrel.
The level would be the highest for Brent, the European benchmark, since Sept. 15. U.S. crude oil also rose to almost $96.

Oil’s renewed rise was briefly halted earlier Monday after reports said that mediators planned to meet with U.S. and Iranian officials separately to discuss the ongoing stalemate between the two sides over the war with Iran. Iran’s semi-official ISNA news agency downplayed the significance of the meetings, saying that Iran’s foreign minister, Abbas Araghchi, would attend talks with mediators, but said no U.S. representatives would be present.
Over the weekend, President Donald Trump said he had rejected a recent proposal from Iran to reopen the Strait of Hormuz, through which critical energy supplies flowed before the war.
“They want to make a deal, and I think that’s fine,” Trump told reporters in Washington. “I like making a deal too, but ... that deal would not be acceptable.”
The momentary pause in oil’s rise, a familiar feature of this year’s turbulent markets, was short-lived.
Bond yields surged to fresh multi-year highs.

By mid-morning, the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield had risen to 5.27%, its highest level since mid-June 2007. A wide swath of other Treasurys also continued to trade above 5%, and the yield on the 30-year bond hit its highest level since May 2004.
The 2-year Treasury, which is often viewed as a signal of where the market expects central bank rates to go, reached its highest level since 2024.
Market watchers’ anxiety has grown alongside the rise in bond yields.

“The significant increase in oil prices so far this year hasn’t knocked the wind out of the global economy’s sails,” longtime market analyst Ed Yardeni wrote Saturday. “The question is whether rapidly rising interest rates will do so.”
“Unfortunately, these higher rates also exacerbate the outlook for large government deficits worldwide,” wrote Yardeni, president of Yardeni Research.
Still, stocks have largely remained resilient in the face of rising inflation from higher oil prices and bond yields that keep shooting higher.

Part of the reason why “is that financial conditions have changed little” since January, said analysts at Goldman Sachs. They added that “the substantial rise in interest rates has been nearly offset by the effects of higher equity prices.”
But the equity market’s rise this year has been driven primarily by just a few sectors, which troubles some analysts.

For the year so far, the S&P 500 has risen a little more than 12%. But a look under the hood reveals a different story. The information technology sector has gained 28% this year and the energy sector has added 38%.
The financial, real estate, utilities, consumer staples, consumer discretionary and communication services sectors have all gained less than 10%.
The health care, industrials and materials sectors are up 10%.

On top of higher oil prices, rising bond yields and geopolitical headlines that could swing stocks in either direction at a moment’s notice, the end of the month features prominent central bank meetings, including at the Federal Reserve, where rates could rise further.

title: Trump to unveil plans for a $15 billion steel mill in Iowa
summary: President Donald Trump will announce a plan for a $15 billion steel mill in Iowa on Monday.
story: President Donald Trump will announce a plan for a $15 billion steel mill in Iowa on Monday.

Mesabi Metallics is building the plant with the aim of starting production by 2030, a White House official said. The facility is expected to produce 10 million tons of steel a year and create as many as 1,750 permanent jobs in the state, the official said.
The plant will be capable of supporting defense sector requirements for high-grade steel, the official said.
The Wall Street Journal was first to report on the new facility.

The plant will use iron ore from a new mine that the company invested $2.5 billion to build in Minnesota. The mine, which will come on line in the coming weeks, will produce about 7.5 million tons of iron per year and create about 350 jobs in the state, the White House official said, noting that it will be the first new iron mine in the U.S. in 50 years.

The mine is based in Minnesota’s Mesabi Iron Range, which stretches 80 to 100 miles and contributed about 60% of total iron ore production in the U.S. during the 20th century, according to the U.S. Geological Survey.

“Trump is delivering on his promise to rebuild American industry, reshore manufacturing, and create new jobs,” White House spokesperson Taylor Rogers said in a statement. “Today’s announcement underscores the President’s historic efforts to revitalize the U.S. steel industry — supporting local communities, strengthening supply chains, and protecting our national security.”

Trump will announce the project at a 2 p.m. ET White House event with Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick, Mesabi Metallics CEO Joe Broking, Export-Import Bank Chairman John Jovanovic and other business leaders.

Jovanovic recently visited the mine, and the Export-Import Bank, the federal government’s export credit agency, will issue up to $10 billion in financing for Mesabi Metallics’ expansion there, an agency release said.

Trump has prioritized the expansion of the U.S. manufacturing sector, including by taking aim at steel imports as part of a wide-ranging trade policy. Although the Supreme Court earlier this year struck down many of the tariffs he imposed, it did leave duties in place on imported steel and aluminum. The U.S. currently levies a 50% tariff on most steel imports.
In a letter to Trump last week, steel industry groups urged the president to “stand firm against efforts to weaken the tariffs” as U.S. steelmakers invest in new mills domestically.
“Weakening the tariffs now would put that progress at risk, threatening American jobs and the economic and national security benefits the policy was designed to protect,” they warned.

title: GoFundMe for Texas man who went viral hauling bags for wife’s cancer bills is removed over ‘factual’ issues
summary: GoFundMe pulled the plug on a campaign to raise money for elderly Texas couple Donald and Josephine Johnson after the husband went viral for delivering luggage to cover his wife’s mounting cancer bills, the platform said Sunday.
story: GoFundMe pulled the plug on a campaign to raise money for an elderly Texas couple after the husband went viral for working a back-breaking job to cover his wife’s mounting bills for cancer treatment, the platform said Sunday.

The digital fundraising site said it “identified factual misrepresentations,” but did not immediately reveal what kind of misrepresentations were behind its decision to end the campaign set to benefit Donald and Josephine Johnson.
The GoFundMe gained national attention and raised nearly $290,000 before it was pulled down.
The campaign was started by a concerned stranger, identified as “Erin H,” who said she spotted on her Ring camera the 81-year-old husband struggling to carry heavy luggage up a flight of stairs.

The organizer said she asked why he working such a physically demanding job at his age, and Johnson said his wife was fighting cancer and this was the only job he could find to pay the overwhelming hospital bills.
But somewhere along the line, GoFundMe said it found “misrepresentations” in the campaign.

“Our Trust & Safety team identified factual misrepresentations, which directly violates our Terms of Service,” the platform said in a statement to NBC News on Sunday. “As a result, the fundraiser has been removed and all donors have been refunded.”
The platform said it has no choice but to take tough action in order to maintain trust with donors.

“Ensuring GoFundMe is a safe and trusted place to give and receive help is our top priority. Taking action like this allows GoFundMe to protect donors’ generosity and our continued ability to support people who are fundraising to help others,” GoFundMe said.

“GoFundMe’s policies, along with those of our payment processors, require authenticity and transparency for donors, and are strictly enforced,” it said. “Because that standard wasn’t met here, donors were protected under our GoFundMe Giving Guarantee, which guarantees a full refund in the rare case something isn’t right.”

title: FBI co-Deputy Director Andrew Bailey steps down after one year on the job
summary: FBI co-Deputy Director Andrew Bailey, who joined the FBI in the newly created position in September 2025 to work alongside then-Deputy Director Dan Bongino, is stepping down, two people familiar with the matter told NBC News.
story: WASHINGTON — Another top FBI official is leaving the bureau after just a year on the job.

Andrew Bailey, who joined the FBI in the newly created position of “co-deputy director” in September 2025 to work alongside then-Deputy Director Dan Bongino, is stepping aside, two people familiar with the matter told NBC News. Bailey confirmed his move later Monday morning on social media.

An internal FBI email said Bailey was leaving for family reasons, the two people familiar with the matter said. Bailey had been the attorney general of Missouri before resigning his position to join the FBI last year. He had worked under FBI Director Kash Patel.
The FBI referred a request for comment to a post Bailey made on social media, stating that he wanted to thank President Donald Trump, Attorney General Todd Blanche and Patel for the opportunity.

“Under President Trump’s leadership, we have delivered historic results in our mission to Make America Safe Again. With great pride in what we have accomplished, I am announcing that I am stepping down to return to my family in Missouri,” Bailey wrote. “I am confident Director Patel will continue to reform the FBI, combat violent crime, defend the homeland, ensure strong organizational accountability, and restore public trust in this institution of excellence.”

Bongino, a conservative podcaster and former Secret Service member, subsequently left his job to return to podcasting after just under a year at the FBI. The nontraditional co-deputy structure, set up when Bongino was in the position, remained in place. Bongino was then replaced by Chris Raia, whose background as a career FBI special agent was more in line with the tradition of having the critical No. 2 position filled by someone with extensive knowledge of the bureau.
MS NOW first reported Bailey’s planned departure.

Patel, who is suing The Atlantic for $250 million over an article about his leadership at the bureau, has recently gotten into heated exchanges with Democratic members of Congress over his leadership at the FBI.

Sack artist Brian Burns injured his knee in the fourth quarter, and with 24 seconds left in regulation, Tennessee moved within 7 yards of a go-ahead touchdown. Instead, the Giants (2-1) survived after Jevon Holland intercepted Titans quarterback Cam Ward.

In Tampa Bay, the Buccaneers played in their franchise-record ninth consecutive one-score game, but Minnesota (3-0) held on, 23-16, after batting down a desperate Hail Mary heave as time expired. For Tampa, what was even more dispiriting than falling to 0-3 was that quarterback Baker Mayfield left with a dislocated thumb that puts his active league-high streak of 54 consecutive starts in jeopardy.

When Cincinnati quarterback Joe Burrow fumbled late in the fourth quarter, Pittsburgh exhaled with a 30-27 win over a division rival. It also breathed a sigh of relief for a different reason. Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers, the NFL’s oldest active player, was showing his age. He entered Sunday having gone seven consecutive starts without throwing multiple touchdown passes. He responded with touchdown passes to three different receivers and led Pittsburgh (2-1) on a game-winning drive that ended with a 33-yard field goal with 2:15 remaining. Burrow’s fumble occurred just before the Bengals (2-1) could reach field-goal range of their own.

With one game remaining in Week 3, six teams remain undefeated after San Francisco edged out a 36-30 win over Arizona. Can the 49ers keep it up, though? A franchise known for suffering a rash of injuries got more bad news Sunday when receiver Mike Evans (ribs) and left tackle Trent Williams (stinger) left the game.

That left the Broncos and Rams to play a vital primetime game — the two Super Bowl contenders each hoping to avoid a second loss within their first three weeks. A pair of controversial defensive pass interference penalties on Denver’s go-ahead drive in the final minute rankled the Rams after the game, but comebacks have become something of a Broncos specialty.

Last season, the Broncos’ 12 comeback wins set an NFL record. Last week, Denver overcame a 10-point deficit to beat Jacksonville. Sunday’s latest rally was the 50th fourth-quarter comeback of coach Sean Payton’s career to move past Mike Tomlin for fourth-most in NFL history. It relied on the 20th touchdown of quarterback Bo Nix’s career when trailing by one score — the most in the league since 2025, when Nix entered the NFL — and resulted in Nix’s seventh career fourth-quarter comeback.
“Just a couple plays short that we left out there,” Rams receiver Konata Mumpfield said.
On a day of wild finishes and tight margins, it was a sentiment shared across the league.

title: Terror suspects arrested near British air base used by U.S. released on bail
summary: LONDON — Police have arrested five British nationals in connection with a massive security operation near a base used by the U.S.
story: LONDON —  Police have arrested five British nationals in connection with a massive security operation near a base used by the U.S. Air Force to facilitate strikes on Iran, the counterterrorism officials running the operation said Monday.

The five men, all from London and in their early to mid-20s, were arrested Sunday on suspicion of terrorism and explosives offenses after three suspicious vehicles were seen moving toward RAF Fairford, a royal air force station about 90 minutes west of London. Dozens of homes were evacuated in the early morning and a large emergency presence was seen around the installation, shaking the normally quiet area in rural Cotswolds.

But after “extensive interviews and inquiries,” the head of Counter Terrorism Policing, Laurence Taylor, said Monday that they had been released on bail, adding that “does not mean that the investigation is over.”
“They are subject to stringent conditions on their movement and contact with others,” he added.

title: Right-wing conservatives push to shut down the last active Jan. 6 prosecution
summary: They say Brian Cole Jr. was framed. The Justice Department is pressing forward with the case.
story: WASHINGTON — There’s just one active federal prosecution still tied to the Jan. 6, 2021, attack on the U.S. Capitol, the case of the man accused of planting two pipe bombs near the Republican National Committee and the Democratic National Committee. And some of MAGA’s most fervent supporters want to shut it down.

Some conservative figures accuse the Trump administration of framing Brian Cole Jr., who was arrested almost five years after the unexploded devices were placed. Cole, as NBC News first reported, told the FBI that he believed the 2020 election had been stolen after false accusations fueled by President Donald Trump and his supporters.

Cole has pleaded not guilty, and a trial is set for February. The FBI said he confessed after his arrest, but his legal team has noted that he was diagnosed with autism and is expected to seek to have the confession tossed based on his disability or argue he was coerced.

The prosecution has opened a rift between the Trump administration and some prominent right-wing conservatives who are seeking to undermine the case by spreading discredited theories about who was to blame. They contend the bombs were placed by “deep state” actors to distract from the police response and make Jan. 6 seem more violent.
Right-wing activists have appeared in court to support Cole, and former Jan. 6 defendants are backing him online.

Trump pardoned Jan. 6 defendants as one of his first acts in office, and as a result, the Justice Department shut down ongoing investigations into the rioters who beat and bloodied law enforcement and caused an estimated $2.7 billion in costs.

Legally, federal prosecutors pushed forward with the pipe bomb case because the devices were placed the night before the attack and therefore the crime wasn’t covered under Trump’s mass Jan. 6 pardon. The devices were viable but didn’t explode, law enforcement said.

Culturally, it’s been a right-wing talking point for years. In a 2024 podcast, Dan Bongino said he had “zero doubt” the bombs were an inside job. When Bongino became the FBI’s deputy director, he pushed the stalled investigation forward. During the announcement of Cole’s arrest, then-Attorney General Pam Bondi credited him with helping crack the case.

Bongino, who left the bureau in January, has not directly addressed how — or whether — his opinions on the “inside job” theory have changed. After the December arrest, he told Fox News commentator Sean Hannity in an interview: “I was paid in the past, Sean, for my opinions, that’s clear, and one day I will be back in that space — but that’s not what I’m paid for now.”

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., publicly posted a photo of officials — including Bondi, U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro, FBI Director Kash Patel and Bongino — at the news conference announcing Cole’s arrest and said they were “complicit” in a conspiracy.

“The evidence is mounting,” Massie said on social media. “All of the people who took credit at the podium upon the arrest of Brian Cole Jr. are complicit, either through negligence or malfeasance. Mr. Cole is not the J5/J6 pipe bomber, and the identity of the actual perpetrator is being obscured. Bookmark it.”

title: Love to Dream just recalled this popular sound machine for fire and burn risk
summary: Love to Dream recalled its portable baby sound machine over a battery fire and burn risk. Here’s how to check your model and date code and get a refund.
story: If you use a Love to Dream sound machine to help your baby drift off, you’ll want to pay attention to this news: The brand has recalled their portable white noise machine because its lithium-ion battery can overheat while charging with an incompatible charger, posing a risk of fire and burns. Below, find everything you need to know about the recall, including how to check whether your sound machine is affected and what to do if it is.
Why was the Love to Dream sound machine recalled?

Love to Dream recalled its Sleep Machine because the device’s lithium-ion battery can overheat while charging if it’s connected to an incompatible charger. That overheating poses a risk of injury from fire and burns, a serious concern for a product that’s often kept in a nursery.

The recall applies only to the Love to Dream Sleep Machine with model number LTD-SM23 and date code 7W15TN. The recalled product is a white, heart-shaped portable white noise machine with a night light and a tan carry strap. You can find the date code printed on the side of the machine or on the back of its box, and Love to Dream says units with any other date code are not affected and aren’t part of the recall.

The affected machines were sold from February 2025 through September 2026, and Love to Dream is conducting the recall in cooperation with the U.S. Consumer Product Safety Commission. The company’s recall notice doesn’t say how many units are affected or whether any overheating incidents or injuries have been reported.
What to do if you have the recalled sound machine

If your Love to Dream Sleep Machine has model number LTD-SM23 and date code 7W15TN, stop using it immediately. Disconnect it from any charger and put it somewhere safe, away from anything flammable or anything that could damage it. Then visit lovetodream.com/recall to find out how to dispose of the device and claim your refund.

Because the machine contains a lithium-ion battery, you should not toss it in your household trash or recycling bin. Instead, dispose of it only according to your local requirements for lithium-ion products.
If you have questions, contact Love to Dream by email at recall@lovetodream.com or call toll-free at 1-833-753-3710.
Other portable sound machines to use instead
The portable sound machines below have not been recalled, and they all have at least a 4.4-star average rating from 1,000 shoppers.
Hatch Go Portable Sound Machine

The Hatch Go is a rechargeable sound machine that you can use while on the go. It plays 10 soothing sounds, like white noise and heartbeat, and has three buttons plus a ring to clip onto a stroller or diaper bag. It needs no app, WiFi or Bluetooth, and lasts up to 15 hours on a single charge.
Yogasleep Hushh Portable White Noise Sound Machine

The Yogasleep Hushh is a compact portable sound machine with three sounds: bright white noise, deep white noise and gentle surf. It weighs just 3.8 ounces so it’s extremely lightweight, has an amber night light and child lock, and clips onto a stroller, car seat or crib. It runs up to 24 hours per charge.
Momcozy Portable Sound Machine with Night Light

With 20 soothing sounds and an amber night light you can dim, this portable machine from Momcozy works for nursery and travel alike. It clips onto a stroller, crib or diaper bag, and includes a timer, child lock and auto shut-off. It charges via USB-C and is designed to last all night.

A towel warmer can do more than just give you cozy vibes, says Michael Tidwell, CEO at Only Towel Warmers, an online towel warmer retailer. “A towel warmer can also serve several other purposes, such as warming the bathroom, drying towels for multiple uses and helping with mold and mildew caused by the wet fabric sitting around.” If you tend to really wet your towels after a shower, this could help you go through fewer towels in a week.

Additionally, if you have a pet that you bathe at home, a warm towel can make the bath process a little less uncomfortable for them. And towel warming racks can be useful for drying bathing suits and other items. So while a towel warmer can feel like it only serves the purpose of luxury, it’s also practical. To help you shop for one, I spoke to Tidwell about what features to consider, then sourced highly-rated options in a range of prices.

Don’t have a ton of floor space? This towel warmer is built to be mounted on the wall and can be hardwired or plugged into an available outlet. I consulted Tidwell for guidance to help you shop for a towel warmer. Since he works for a retailer that sells towel warmers, I did not ask him for product recommendations. Here are the features recommended to keep in mind when shopping for a towel warmer:

Type: There are wall-mounted towel warming racks and freestanding warming racks that you hang towels on. There are also bucket-style warmers that you place towels in to warm them up. When choosing between these, consider the space you have. A standing towel rack will take up the most space, whereas a wall-mounted rack will take up the least floor space. Bucket warmers take up a similar amount of space as a small trash can. Size: Towel warmers are mostly found in small and large sizes. title: GoFundMe for Texas man who went viral hauling bags for wife’s cancer bills is removed over ‘factual’ issues
summary: GoFundMe pulled the plug on a campaign to raise money for elderly Texas couple Donald and Josephine Johnson after the husband went viral for delivering luggage to cover his wife’s mounting cancer bills, the platform said Sunday.
story: GoFundMe pulled the plug on a campaign to raise money for an elderly Texas couple after the husband went viral for working a back-breaking job to cover his wife’s mounting bills for cancer treatment, the platform said Sunday.

The digital fundraising site said it “identified factual misrepresentations,” but did not immediately reveal what kind of misrepresentations were behind its decision to end the campaign set to benefit Donald and Josephine Johnson.
The GoFundMe gained national attention and raised nearly $290,000 before it was pulled down.
The campaign was started by a concerned stranger, identified as “Erin H,” who said she spotted on her Ring camera the 81-year-old husband struggling to carry heavy luggage up a flight of stairs.

The organizer said she asked why he working such a physically demanding job at his age, and Johnson said his wife was fighting cancer and this was the only job he could find to pay the overwhelming hospital bills.
But somewhere along the line, GoFundMe said it found “misrepresentations” in the campaign.

“Our Trust & Safety team identified factual misrepresentations, which directly violates our Terms of Service,” the platform said in a statement to NBC News on Sunday. “As a result, the fundraiser has been removed and all donors have been refunded.”
The platform said it has no choice but to take tough action in order to maintain trust with donors.

“Ensuring GoFundMe is a safe and trusted place to give and receive help is our top priority. Taking action like this allows GoFundMe to protect donors’ generosity and our continued ability to support people who are fundraising to help others,” GoFundMe said.

“GoFundMe’s policies, along with those of our payment processors, require authenticity and transparency for donors, and are strictly enforced,” it said. “Because that standard wasn’t met here, donors were protected under our GoFundMe Giving Guarantee, which guarantees a full refund in the rare case something isn’t right.”

title: BASE jumper fatally plunges 700 feet after wingsuit failure in Utah
summary: Authorities described the 27-year-old man, whose identity wasn’t released, as experienced in the endeavor.
story: A 27-year-old BASE jumper died Sunday after his wingsuit failed when he launched from a 700-foot perch in Utah, authorities said.

The man, whose identity was withheld until his family could be notified, fatally plunged from a mountainous area of Hyrum, Utah, east of Millville Canyon and east of the small city of Millville, Cache County Chief Sheriff’s Deputy Doyle Peck said.

Search-and-rescue crews were called to Leetham’s Hollow, an area of canyon walls and cliffs not unlike the Grand Canyon’s, at 9:10 a.m. Sunday and declared the man dead at the scene, Peck said in a statement.
“On today’s jump, something went wrong and he did not have enough lift with his wingsuit,” Peck said. “He impacted the ground at a high rate of speed resulting in his death.”
The man was “experienced in this type of activity” and was part of a group of as many as 10 people who appeared to be engaged in wingsuit-aided BASE jumping, according to Peck.
The area, about 45 miles north of Ogden, is popular with BASE jumpers, he said.
A medical transport helicopter sent to help with the initial search transported the man’s body, Peck said.

Before Sunday, 541 deaths around the world since 1981 had been logged by the BASE Fatality List, maintained by an online community for the sport. This year, 15 such deaths have been reported globally, according to the list.
In June, two BASE jumpers died in a separate accident in Utah. One of them, Andy Lewis, performed onstage with Madonna at the 2012 Super Bowl.

Photographer Carl Boenish helped coin BASE as a description of the sport’s adrenaline-inspiring launch points (buildings, antennas, spans, earth) in 1978, when he videotaped early jumps from Yosemite National Park’s El Capitan rock formation.

title: The Best Dressed Stars of the 2026 VMAs, According to 3 Fashion Experts
summary: Who are the best dressed stars from the VMAs 2026 red carpet? We asked three fashion experts
story: If there’s one red carpet where fashion rules are meant to be broken, it’s the MTV VMAs.

She also loved the fabric’s subtle sheen, noting that “that’s atypical for menswear and works so well here!”
Normani
Normani’s ensemble struck DuRocher as a cool mix of sexy, feminine and fashion forward.

“I love the combination of that jersey-like, leather-inspired look with the dramatic flower at the dropped torso and the fit-and-flare silhouette,” she says. “It feels cool and fashion-forward while still being very feminine.”
For DuRocher, the overall effect is “modern pageant glamour in the best way.”
Carter Gregory
Carter Gregory, vice president of A&R at Capitol Music Group, leaned fully into rock-and-roll glamour in archival Tom Ford.
“Carter Gregory wearing archival Tom Ford was peak rock and roll,” Gillette says. She points to the leather pants and leopard print as a particularly bold combination.
The unexpected color combination also kept the ensemble feeling contemporary. The black and brown, she says, “kept this look feeling fashion forward and modern.”
Teyana Taylor
Teyana Taylor knows how to make an entrance, and both fashion experts took notice.

Gillette called Taylor’s Zuhair Murad Couture look “gothic glam at its finest,” pointing to the crochet-inspired fabric, dramatic neckline and lush feather details. The result, she says, was “red carpet alchemy.”
DuRocher was equally enthusiastic about Taylor’s revealing gown.

“This is how you wear a revealing dress to an awards show, it’s provocative, but it still feels elegant,” she says. “I love the lace and beaded detailing and the way the look plays with coverage and skin.”
Nicky Hilton
DuRocher immediately noticed the rhinestones, sheer detailing and form-fitting silhouette.
“I especially love the detail in the back. The dress itself is a wow moment,” she says.
Lisa Rinna
Lisa Rinna brought a little ’80s glamour to the VMAs, and DuRocher was here for it.
“I love the white dress paired with her short, bleached hair, the entire look feels very ’80s in the best possible way,” she says.
It’s the cohesion of the styling that really works for her. “Everything works together, from the styling to the silhouette, and she looks completely put together,” DuRocher says.
Olandria Carthen
The “Love Island” star brought early-2000s pop-star energy to the VMAs in a lace-up MMS look.
“Olandria seemed to be channeling a pop star from the early aughts in this laced up MMS look that hit on both the textural and corseting trends we saw all over the red carpet tonight,” Gillette says.
She could even picture a certain pop icon in it: “I could absolutely see Christina Aguilera wearing something like this to the VMAs 25 years ago.”
Gillette also loved the way Carthen modernized the look with the red details and feminine bow at the hem, which played against the tougher leather.
Sienna Spiro
Sienna Spiro, who won the award for best new artist, caught DuRocher’s eye for an entirely different reason: intricate femininity.
“Sienna Spiro’s gown is so intricate and delicate,” she says. “I love the detailing throughout the dress and the way it feels incredibly feminine while still making an impact on the carpet.”
“The shape and embellishment give it a beautiful sense of glamour without feeling overdone,” DuRocher says.
Lisa
Lisa made a case for red and then doubled down with an oversized matching jacket.
“Lisa looks spectacular,” DuRocher says. “I love the red dress paired with that big, oversized red jacket, it feels bold, glamorous and incredibly current.”
She also sees the outfit as a snapshot of two major trends coming together. “Red is having such a moment right now, and so is lace, so I love seeing those trends come together here.”
Troye Sivan
Troye Sivan, the Australian singer, took a more unexpected approach in Erdem, and Gillette loved the contrast.

“The interplay between the masculine suit with the very high almost Edwardian collar against the draped silk and feathers is such a strong contrast especially since everything is in black and super crisp optic white,” she says.
Taylor Swift
“There’s something deliciously dark about this,” Paige says. “It’s almost ‘Practical Magic’ witchery, but rendered in liquid shimmer.”

The juxtaposition gives the look a sense of “sorceress” glamour, while the silver draping adds a touch of disco, she says. The asymmetry, Paige adds, keeps all that drama in Tamara Ralph’s couture collectionfeeling effortless rather than overworked.
Shaboozey

“Entirely rock star,” Paige says. “The leather three-piece could have gone costume very quickly, but the lean proportions, skinny tie, statement buckle and cropped trouser keep it feeling intentional rather than too theatrical.”

The combination gives the look an “outlaw-meets-frontman energy,” she says. The result feels polished without losing its edge, “like he might accept an award and then immediately disappear onto a tour bus.”

title: How Many VMAs Has Taylor Swift Won?
summary: How many VMAs does Taylor Swift have? She just set a record by winning 33.
story: Taylor Swift has a long history with the MTV VMAs and just broke yet another record.
Swift received her 33rd moon person at the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards, becoming the most-awarded artist in VMAs history. She was previously tied with Beyoncé with 30 awards.

Swift won three VMAs at the 2026 ceremony on Sept. 27, including the inaugural Artist Director Honors, which honors artists’ work behind the camera to make music videos. In her acceptance speech, Swift said she’s made 60 music videos and wrote and directed 18.

Swift also won the VMA for best direction for “Opalite” and the night’s marquee award, video of the year, for “The Fate of Ophelia.” Both tracks are from her 12th studio album “The Life of a Showgirl,” which was just rereleased as a special “The Encore” edition with four new tracks.
Swift became the most awarded solo artist in VMAs history after the 2024 ceremony, at which she won seven total trophies. That brought her career total to 30, tying her with Beyoncé at the time.
Beyoncé has won 26 VMAs as a solo artist, two with Destiny’s Child and two with her husband, Jay-Z, as The Carters, according to the Guinness Book of World Records.

title: ‘Zoolander’ Turns 25: Ben Stiller Promoted His Comedy on TODAY in 2001 After a Heavy Time for the Country
summary: In 2001, Ben Stiller spoke with TODAY about “Zoolander” coming out less than three weeks after the Sept. 11 terror attacks.
story: Welcome to the “TODAY Archives,” where we revisit memories from our show when celebrities and newsmakers started discourse, made us laugh or shaped our culture. This latest installment highlights Ben Stiller, who stopped by the show on Sept. 28, 2001 to talk about his movie “Zoolander,” which came out in the wake of the Sept. 11 terror attacks.

Comedy was in an unprecedented situation of uncertainty after the events of Sept. 11. No one knew when, or if, the country would be ready to laugh again, as a reeling country continued to mourn the terror attacks. It was into this uncharted environment that Ben Stiller found himself when “Zoolander” was released in theaters on Sept. 28, 2001.

That same day, Stiller appeared on TODAY with Katie Couric, not just to talk about the film that poked fun at the modeling industry, but also the circumstances under which it would be served up to the public.
“You’re hoping to provide people with some much needed escapism,” Couric said.
“Yeah, just (a) distraction,” Stiller replied.

As it turned out, there was an appetite for comedy and Derek Zoolander’s famed “Blue Steel” gaze. The movie would open in second place, en route to a $45 million take at the domestic box office. The film eventually became a favorite in the Stiller canon and spawned a sequel in 2016.
What Did Ben Stiller Say About Releasing ‘Zoolander’ After 9/11?

“It’s a really strange time to just be talking about movies and entertainment because it just all kind of does seem frivolous,” he said. “For me, like having the movie come out now, the toughest thing about it. I thought it was a good idea to be able to have a comedy for people to go to if they wanted to, to have that option. But talking about it seems kind of not important.”
Stiller, who co-wrote, co-produced, starred in and directed “Zoolander,” called it a “really silly, ridiculous comedy” that he had seen since the attacks, but before it was officially released.

“Everything is different now,” he said. “But the great thing about seeing it, I’ve seen it with some audiences since this, and people are laughing. And it does seem to at least kind of be so silly that it kind of takes them out of stuff for awhile. But, definitely, everything’s different now.”
What Did Ben Stiller Think About Skewering the Fashion Industry?

When it came to poking fun at the fashion industry, Stiller said, “I can relate to it because we, in show business, I think sometimes take ourselves a little too seriously, get wrapped up in our own craziness.”
Adding, “In a way, it’s kind of like, working out some of those demons, not just kind of making fun of the modeling industry because that’s pretty easy.”
How Did ‘Zoolander’ Land So Many Celebrity Cameos?

“Zoolander” featured some serious star power in small roles. David Bowie, Lenny Kravitz, Winona Ryder, Gwen Stefani, Christian Slater, Donald Trump and Lance Bass are just some of the people who had cameos.
“Everybody kind of wanted to just have fun. It’s a real, like I said, it’s a silly movie, so they read the script and it just kind of felt like a fun thing to do,” Stiller said.

title: Adam Lambert Shocks Crowd With Surprise Performance During VMAs George Michael Tribute
summary: The MTV Video Music Awards paid tribute to icon George Michael with a medley that featured some of the icon’s biggest hits. While the performance featured several big names, the highlight was a soulful cover of Michael’s “Freedom! ‘90,” led by Adam Lambert, whose appearance was not announced ahead of the ceremony.
story: Surprise!

The MTV Video Music Awards paid tribute to icon George Michael with a medley that featured some of the icon’s biggest hits. While the performance featured several big names, the highlight was a soulful cover of Michael’s “Freedom! ‘90,” led by Adam Lambert, whose appearance was not announced ahead of the ceremony.
The homage comes a decade after the pop legend and queer icon died on Christmas Day 2016 at age 53.
Lambert, joined by several other artists including singer Meek and MNEK, belted out the 1990 hit. Several in the crowd were brought to their feet during the performance.

The tribute also featured Sombr, who performed Michael’s hit songs “Faith” and “Father Figure,” Raye, who performed “Knew You Were Waiting,” and Teddy Swims who sang a rendition of “Careless Whisper.”
During his portion, Sombr also wore a black Harley-Davidson jacket that originally worn by Michael during his 1988 Faith Tour, according to Vogue.
“To wear a jacket that has become so synonymous with that era was pretty surreal, and an honor,” Sombr told the magazine.

Michael, who won a host of VMAs, including the Video Vanguard lifetime achievement award in 1989, was highly regarded as a pioneering artist in the pop music scene, making a significant impact both as one-half of the duo Wham! and also as a solo artist.
While the icon was known for his many musical hits, he is also remembered as a champion of the LGBTQ+ community and philanthropist, who used his platform to help find a cure for HIV and AIDS.

Michael was outed as gay in 1998 following an incident in Beverly Hills during which he was arrested for engaging in a lewd act at a public toilet. Michael later roasted the ordeal in his music video for “Outside,” in which he mocked the Los Angeles police officers who caught him by featuring two uniformed officers kissing.

“I’m a very proud man. I want people to know that I have not been exposed as a gay man,” Michael told CNN in a now-famous 1998 interview. “I don’t feel any shame whatsoever, and neither do I think I should.”
With his unapologetic embrace of his sexuality, the musician is credited with opening the door and empowering many other queer entertainers in the music industry.

Given his rich legacy, many fans initially called out the VMAs for its choice in tribute performers — none of whom had publicly identified as a member of the LGBTQ+ community. MTV had announced exclusively in Rolling Stone Sept. 22 that acts Raye, Sombr and Teddy Swims would be performing. Many felt that without performers who reflected Michael’s activism and identity, the LGBTQ community was being snubbed.

“You’d think with George being an icon for the LGBT community, they’d get someone like Sam Smith or Troye Sivan involved,” one user wrote on social media platform Reddit, referencing other openly gay pop icons.
While no other artists were announced ahead of the awards, singer Adam Lambert posted a cryptic Instagram story which featured Michael’s song “Freedom ‘90.”

title: A Brief History of Madonna and the VMAs, Going Back to 1984: ‘The House She Helped Build’
summary: Madonna is returning to the VMAs. What is Madonna’s history with the VMAs?
story: “Catch Me Up” is a TODAY series where our experts and journalists bring readers up to speed on the day’s biggest headlines.
Where would the MTV Video Music Awards be without Madonna?

Madonna’s name is practically synonymous with the VMAs. She was there from the beginning, rolling around the stage in a wedding dress while performing “Like A Virgin” during the awards show’s 1984 debut.

Over the next four decades, Madonna returned to the VMAs to deliver groundbreaking performances. She’s also made headlines with outrageous antics — like French kissing Britney Spears onstage — and touched fans’ hearts with an emotional tribute to Michael Jackson after the musician’s death in 2009.
Now, the Queen of Pop is poised make a historic return to the 2026 VMAs on Sept. 27 when she performs at the awards show for the first time in 23 years.
Madonna’s performance will kick off the awards show for a record-breaking fifth time, ending her tie with Rihanna, who’s opened the show four times.
Madonna who released her hit album, “Confessions II,” in July, also goes into this year’s VMAs as the most nominated performer.
The singer is “returning to sit on her throne for the night,” NBC News entertainment contributor Chris Witherspoon tells TODAY.com.

“You simply cannot tell the story of the VMAs without telling the story of Madonna. From ‘Like a Virgin’ in 1984, to ‘Vogue’ in 1990, to that unforgettable 2003 performance with Britney Spears, Christina Aguilera and Missy Elliott, Madonna understood the assignment before we even had the phrase,” said Witherspoon.
“Madonna returning to the VMAs doesn’t feel like a comeback to me. It feels like the Queen of Pop returning to the house she helped build,” Witherspoon added.
Ahead of Madonna’s triumphant VMAs return, let’s take a look back at her 10 biggest moments at the awards show.
1) The Wedding Dress Seen Round the World (1984)

Madonna’s audacious performance at the inaugural MTV Video Music Awards in 1984 — she rolled around the stage in a punky ensemble that includes a wedding dress, rosary beads and a “Boy Toy” belt buckle — became her breakout moment.
The raunchy performance, which also included some bumping and grinding, also branded the VMAs as a rebellious alternative to the Grammys and other awards shows.

“MTV could barely fill the seats at the VMAs in year one. By year two, pretty much every act wanted a spot on that stage. Madonna was at the first show in 1984, rolling across the stage in a wedding dress singing ‘Like a Virgin.’ I’d give her a lot of credit for that turnaround,” Jeff Moore, a music marketing strategist, professor, and former touring musician, told TODAY.com.
2) Madonna Expresses Herself (1989)
Madonna returned to the VMAs five years later to deliver one of her finest televised performances when she sang “Express Yourself” with her two backup singers-dancers.

The newly divorced singer — her marriage to Sean Penn officially ended earlier in the year —  began her high-energy, tightly choreographed performance wearing a dark suit before stripping down to a corset.
3) ‘Vogue’ Meets the French Revolution (1990)

The former Material Girl’s breathtaking 1990 performance of “Vogue” was inspired by the French Revolution. Madge as Marie Antoinette? Oh, it worked, right down to her and her dancers’ 18th century-style powdered wigs, heavy white face makeup and corseted gowns.
4) ‘Ray of Light’ with Lenny Kravtiz (1998)
In what’s considered one of the best live performances, Madonna showed off her vocal chops on the soaring “Ray of Light’ with guest guitarist Lenny Kravitz during the 1998 show.
The singer, who kicked off the performance with the Hindu-inspired  “Shanti Ashtangi,” also swept the awards that night, taking home five Moon Man trophies.
5) Madonna Meets Her Drag Impersonators (1999)
The singer was feted the following year by a group of drag queens who wore some of her most memorable looks as they lip-synched and danced to her greatest hits.
“All I have to say is that it takes a real man to fill my shoes!” the singer quipped afterwards.
6) Kissing Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera (2003)
In 2003, Madonna shocked viewers when she took a moment during a throwback performance of “Like A Virgin” to kiss shared her guest performers Britney Spears and Christina Aguilera.
Spears and Aguilera donned skimpy wedding dress looks in a fun nod to Madonna’s debut VMAs performance.
7) An Emotional Tribute to Michael Jackson (2009)

Madonna showed off her serious side when she paid an emotional tribute to her late fellow pop icon Michael Jackson at the 2009 VMAs, calling Jackson “one of the greatest talents the world has ever known.”

“His music,” she said in her speech, “had an extra layer of inexplicable magic that didn’t just make you want to dance but actually made you believe you could fly, dare to dream, be anything that you wanted to be.”
She also recalled going to dinner with Jackson years before.

“Later we went back to my house to watch a movie and sat on the couch like two kids, and somewhere in the middle of the movie, his hand snuck over and held mine,” she said. “It felt like he was looking for more of a friend than a romance, and I was happy to oblige. In that moment, he didn’t feel like a superstar. He felt like a human being.”
8) A Surprise Appearance, Motherf-----! (2021)
Decked out out black dominatrix bodysuit and cap, Madonna made a surprise appearance to open the 2021 VMAs.
The singer’s appearance came just after viewers watched a short video telling the story of her arrival in New York City decades before with just $35 to her name.
Madonna then walked out onstage, telling the crowd, “And they said we wouldn’t last. But we’re still here, motherf------!”

story: The MTV VMAs have always been known for some outrageous looks. And this year, one particular artist’s outfit is definitely creating some conversation.

Sombr arrived at the ceremony Sept. 27, wearing a long, striped furry jacket from ERL, no shirt and pair of black leather pants that were held together by a belt with the word “SEX” across it. And people aren’t quite sure what to think.
“this is not the serve he thought this was,” one person wrote on social media platform X.
Another internet user thought he crushed it.
“sorry yall he ate down 😭” the individual wrote on X.

Sombr is slated to perform during the tribute to late pop icon George Michael. He was announced as one of several other acts, including Raye and Teddy Swims who will be paying homage to the “Freedom! ‘90” singer, who died a decade ago on Christmas day.

Sombr joins a long list of artists who have shocked the world with their VMAs outfits. Lady Gaga, for example, turned heads at the 2010 ceremony with her famous dress made completely out of meat. And Miley Cyrus made headlines with her quite revealing Versace suspenders look when she hosted the awards in 2015.

The 2026 MTV Video Music Awards are being hosted by Snoop Dogg at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Madonna leads with 11 nominations. The show will feature special presentations, like the MTV VMA Artist Director Honors and Video Vanguard Award. Taylor Swift, who received nine nominations, will receive the Artist Director Honors award and debut the music video for her new single “Patient Zero.” The ceremony will include tributes to Dolly Parton and George Michael, as well.

title: Is Taylor Swift’s 2026 VMAs Dress a Nod to Her ‘Patient Zero’ Music Video?
summary: What did Taylor Swift wear to the VMAs and does it have a hidden meaning? Here’s what to know
story: Taylor Swift is back at the VMAs for the first time in two years. She arrived at the red carpet shortly before the award show’s 7:30  p.m. ET start time wearing a sleek black and silver dress.

The Tamara Ralph couture gown started with a tight-fitted black bodice and a high neck, before transitioning into a cascading, shimmering skirt. She paired it with long earrings and her new shorter haircut.

The contrasting vibe of the dress seems to be a nod to the “Patient Zero” music video, which she’s debuting in full at the 2026 VMAs. The music video’s somber and dark visuals were already teased ahead of the show, and accompany lyrics about a toxic relationship.
The dress is also reminiscent of cover art visuals released along with the single, which show Swift in a black dress with a high neckline.
Her husband, Travis Kelce, wasn’t with her at the red carpet, as he has a football game against the Miami Dolphins in Florida at the same time as the VMAs.
Swift was last at the awards show in 2024, rounding out an eventful three-year span in which she announced surprise albums and swept categories.
This year, she’s being honored with the inaugural MTV VMA Artist Director Honors.

Swift wore a yellow-and-black plaid get-up to her last VMAs in 2024, where she was up for 12 awards. Swift won seven awards that night, and thanked her now-husband Kelce in her speech for video of the year.
“Everything this man touches turns to happiness and fun and magic,” she said. “So I want to thank him for adding that to our shoot because I will always remember that.”
The year before, in 2023, Swift had another astonishing VMAs, tying the record for most wins in one night.
And in 2022, she made a surprise appearance and announced a new album.
That year, she wore a dress that was fit for a showgirl, an era that would only come out three years later.

The 2026 MTV Video Music Awards are being hosted by Snoop Dogg at the Peacock Theater in Los Angeles. Madonna leads with 11 nominations. The show will feature special presentations, like the MTV VMA Artist Director Honors and Video Vanguard Award. Taylor Swift, who received nine nominations, will receive the Artist Director Honors award and debut the music video for her new single “Patient Zero.” The ceremony will include tributes to Dolly Parton and George Michael, as well.

title: ‘Love Island USA’ Alums Stun At The MTV VMAs Red Carpet
summary: Several former cast members of “Love Island USA” showed up to the MTV Video Music Awards red carpet Sept. 27 with looks that would make anyone’s head turn.
story: The islanders did not come to play.
Several former cast members of “Love Island USA” showed up to the MTV Video Music Awards red carpet Sept. 27 with looks that would make anyone’s head turn.

The ceremony, which will be hosted by rapper Snoop Dogg, is being held at the Peacock Theater in downtown Los Angeles. Olandria Carthen, a breakout star from Season 7 of the Peacock reality competition show, strutted the carpet wearing a bodysuit and mermaid skirt from ManMadeSkins for a sultry, gothic look.
Meanwhile her ex and fellow Season 7 alum Nicolas Vansteenberghe rocked a monochromatic, off-white outfit. He told E! News that he did not at all mind running into his former flame at the ceremony.
“We have a lot of love for each other,” he said. “We’re constantly supporting each other. I’ll always be her number one fan.”
Aniya Harvey, a finalist in the most recent season of “Love Island USA,” stunned in a short, shimmering halter-top gown resembling a chandelier.
From the looks of it, they all deserved to be coupled up by the fire pit!

title: What Time Are the VMAs Tonight? How to Watch the 2026 VMAs
summary: When do the 2026 VMAs start? What is the start time of the 2026 VMAs? Here’s how to watch the awards show and what channel they’re on.
story: It’s that time of year again for music’s biggest stars to take the stage for the 2026 MTV Video Music Awards.

The annual award show returns this Sunday, Sept. 27, and will highlight some of the biggest artists, songs and performances voted on by fans over the last year. Snoop Dogg is hosting this year’s festivities in Los Angeles for the first time, other notable award presenters such as Teyana Taylor and Charli xcx.
See all the arrivals at the 2026 VMAs.

In addition to awards, the night will also feature a star-studded lineup of performances. Among those taking the stage are Madonna, kicking off the night, and Sienna Spiro, Lisa and Shaboozey, to name a few.

This year’s ceremony will honor two music legends with special tribute performances. Kacey Musgraves will pay tribute to late country singer Dolly Parton, while RAYE, Sombr and Teddy Swims will honor artist George Michael.

Whether you’re tuning in for the performances, hoping to see your favorite artist take home an award, or simply need a glimpse at this year’s fashion choices, here’s everything you need to know about how to watch the 2026 VMAs.
When Are the 2026 VMAs?
The 2026 VMAs will take place on Sunday, Sept. 27.
What Time Are the 2026 VMAs?
The VMAs will begin at 7:30 p.m. ET/4:30 p.m. PT. This year’s show is scheduled to run about two hours.
How to Watch the 2026 VMAs
The VMAs will be broadcast live Sunday night on MTV and CBS, with live streaming available on Paramount+ with a subscription to the Paramount+ Premium plan.
How to Vote for the 2026 VMAs
Viewers over the age of 13 can cast votes for their favorites by visiting MTV’s official voting site. Each person is allowed up to 10 votes each day per category.
Voting for most categories closed Friday, Sept. 25, with the exception of best new artist, which ends on the day of the VMAs, Sunday, Sept. 27.

title: Why Is Travis Kelce Not Going to the 2026 VMAs? His Absence, Explained
summary: Travis Kelce won’t be attending the VMAs with Taylor Swift for an obvious reason. It’s the same night as the Chiefs game against the Dolphins.
story: It’s a big night for Taylor Swift amid this year’s MTV Video Music Awards. And unfortunately her beau won’t be able to join her.
While Swift is slated to receive the inaugural Artist Director Honors at ceremony at the Peacock Theater in downtown Los Angeles, her hubby Travis Kelce will be across the country in Miami, Florida.

Kelce, a tight-end for the Kansas City Chiefs, just wrapped up a game Sept. 27 against the Miami Dolphins in Florida. The Chiefs took the win 24-10. Among the highlights was Kelce’s 48-yard catch-and-run that opened the game.

For Swift, the VMAs, which will be hosted by Snoop Dogg, will not only be a memorable one because of the Artist Director Honors. She’s also up for several awards including video of the year, artist of the year and best album.
In July, Swift and Kelce tied the knot at New York’s Madison Square Garden in one of the most high-profile weddings of the year. Since, the pair have been openly gushing about their newlywed status.

Most recently during the Sept. 20 Kansas City Chiefs game against the Indianapolis Colts, Swift responded to Kelce’s first touchdown of the season by pointing at her engagement ring and wedding band and saying, “That’s my husband!”
